paper_metadata.title: Solving General QUBOs with Warm-Start QAOA via a Reduction to Max-Cut

experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA using Goemans-Williamson SDP relaxation projected to 2 dimensions (GW2) on QUBO instances mapped to Max-Cut, evaluated on random QUBOs, TSP, portfolio optimization, and MIS with different vertex-at-top rotations.

algorithm.variant: Warm-start QAOA with GW2 SDP initialization via QUBO-to-Max-Cut reduction
algorithm.ansatz: Warm-started QAOA with custom mixer / separable initial state
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed-depth evaluation at p = 0,1,2,3,4,5; optimizer run 10 times per circuit and best run selected
algorithm.parameter_initialization: For p=1, parameters drawn uniformly; for p>1, 9 initializations drawn uniformly and 1 initialized from best parameters at depth p-1

problem_formulation.encoding_details: QUBO instances are reduced to Max-Cut by introducing one auxiliary variable/qubit; each QUBO has 16 binary variables and maps to a 17-vertex Max-Cut graph
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize x^T Q x; evaluated via equivalent Max-Cut Ising Hamiltonian after reduction
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints for generic QUBO; TSP and MIS are encoded with penalty terms in the QUBO formulation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_Q = sum_{i,j} Q_ij ((1 - Z_i)/2)((1 - Z_j)/2); after reduction, H_M = -(1/4) sum_{i,j} A_ij Z_i Z_j

problem_instance.description: Benchmark suite of 16-variable QUBOs: continuous random QUBOs, discrete random QUBOs, 5-city TSP, portfolio optimization, MIS on Erdős–Rényi and Newman–Watts–Strogatz graphs

dataset_specification.description: 1000 instances per problem type; random QUBOs sampled from symmetric matrices with upper-triangular entries from U[-1,1] or {−1,1}; TSP uses 5 random points in [-1,1]^2; portfolio uses geometric Brownian motion with n=16 assets and N=250 time steps; MIS uses n=16 graphs from GNP(p=0.25) and NWS(k=3,p=0.5)

implementation_details.classical_solver: L-BFGS-B for GW relaxation; COBYLA for QAOA parameter optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Solve GW SDP relaxation; project vectors to 2D; apply vertex-at-top rotation; for QUBO-to-Max-Cut mapping, construct corresponding graph with one auxiliary vertex
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure optimized QAOA state; compute instance-specific approximation ratio and optimal sampling probability

speedup_claims.conditions: No explicit speedup or complexity advantage is claimed; the paper reports empirical performance comparisons only.
speedup_claims.caveats: Results are benchmark-specific and do not establish asymptotic advantage.

experiments.description: Warm-start QAOA using direct QUBO relaxation (Egger et al. style) on the same benchmark suite, with 10 and 50 random initializations for the nonconvex cases.

algorithm.ansatz: Warm-started QAOA with separable initial state
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Fixed-depth evaluation at p = 0,1,2,3,4,5; optimizer run 10 times per circuit and best run selected
algorithm.parameter_initialization: For general QUBOs, the continuous relaxation y^T Q y over [0,1]^n is estimated by local optimization from random initial points in [0,1]^n; the resulting y_c is converted to single-qubit RY angles with clipping by epsilon

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Direct relaxation of QUBO variables x_i in {0,1} to y_i in [0,1], then map each variable to a single qubit via RY(θ_i)|0⟩
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize y^T Q y over y in [0,1]^n as a relaxation of max x^T Q x
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints for generic QUBO; TSP and MIS are encoded with penalty terms in the QUBO formulation

problem_instance.description: Benchmark suite of 16-variable QUBOs: continuous random QUBOs, discrete random QUBOs, 5-city TSP, portfolio optimization, MIS on Erdős–Rényi and Newman–Watts–Strogatz graphs

dataset_specification.description: 1000 instances per problem type; random QUBOs sampled from symmetric matrices with upper-triangular entries from U[-1,1] or {−1,1}; TSP uses 5 random points in [-1,1]^2; portfolio uses geometric Brownian motion with n=16 assets and N=250 time steps; MIS uses n=16 graphs from GNP(p=0.25) and NWS(k=3,p=0.5)

implementation_details.classical_solver: L-BFGS-B for the continuous relaxation; COBYLA for QAOA parameter optimization
implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Solve or approximate the QUBO relaxation with random restarts; clip relaxation variables using epsilon; convert to warm-start single-qubit RY states
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure optimized QAOA state; compute instance-specific approximation ratio and optimal sampling probability

speedup_claims.conditions: No explicit speedup or complexity advantage is claimed; the paper reports empirical performance comparisons only.
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper notes that QUBO-relaxed performance depends strongly on the number of random initializations; for portfolio optimization, the relaxation is convex and the number of initializations does not matter.
